Earth Intelligence &
Environmental Analytics

EarthTrend delivers rigorous empirical climate trend statistics from NASA Earth observations. Powered by 28,080 verified historical observations (2000–2025) across Egypt and live NASA POWER API integration worldwide.

The 5 Core Scientific Questions

Every analysis provides mathematical, peer-tested answers to the fundamental Earth science questions.

1. WHAT is changing?

Environmental Variables

Air Temperature (T2M), Precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), and All-Sky Solar Irradiance calibrated via MERRA-2 and CERES.

2. WHERE is it changing?

Geographical Precision

Interactive global map targeting, with dense 30-station verified grid across the Nile Delta, Cairo, Alexandria, and Suez Canal.

3. HOW MUCH is it changing?

Quantitative Rates

Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression slope and robust Theil-Sen median slopes reported in physical units per year and per decade.

4. HOW does it change over time?

Temporal Dynamics

Decomposes 26 years of monthly records (2000-2025), removing 12-month cyclical noise to evaluate baseline anomaly trajectories.

5. IS it statistically significant?

Hypothesis Testing

Two-sided p-values and Mann-Kendall monotonic trend tests evaluated at α = 0.05 with exact 95% confidence bands.

Ethical Transparency

No data fabrication. Inconclusive tests are never falsely described as proof of no environmental change.

About EarthTrend

Empirical environmental analytics delivering transparent answers using real NASA observations.

Scientific Methodology

Ordinary Least Squares (OLS): Fits y(t) = β₀ + β₁t + ε (t in elapsed years). Calculates rate of change per year and decade with exact 95% confidence intervals.

Mann-Kendall Test: Non-parametric rank correlation evaluating monotonic trend direction and tie-corrected Z statistics.

Theil-Sen Estimator: Median of all pairwise slopes, offering resilience against transient sensor spikes or anomalous years.

Seasonal Adjustment: Subtracts 12-month calendar baseline climatology to expose underlying multi-decadal trends.

Data Attribution

Primary historical variables originate from the NASA POWER project (NASA Langley Research Center) derived from MERRA-2 reanalysis and CERES satellite observations. Digital elevation and land-cover context are provided by NASADEM and ESA WorldCover as static reference layers.
